speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly how your right groin pain started, especially regarding the rear-end collision and any abnormal positioning of your leg afterward. Also, have you noticed any difficulty walking or moving your leg since the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The immediate onset of right groin pain and knee pain following a rear-end collision is concerning for an acetabular fracture or hip dislocation. Did you experience any deformity of the right hip or leg immediately after the accident, such as the leg appearing shortened or turned outward? Also, is the pain significantly worse with any attempt to move your leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a rear-end collision is pathognomonic for this injury. I will confirm this with imaging immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_X-Ray.
